CREATE SEQUENCE defaults_seen

CREATE TABLE inputs(id integer PRIMARY KEY, v integer)
INSERT INTO inputs VALUES (1, 2), (2, NULL), (3, 4)
CREATE FUNCTION live_check(v integer) RETURNS boolean LANGUAGE SQL VOLATILE AS 'SELECT nextval(''checks_seen'') > 0 AND (v IS NULL OR v >= 0)'
CREATE DOMAIN accepted_value AS integer CHECK (live_check(VALUE))
CREATE FUNCTION domain_input(a accepted_value) RETURNS SETOF integer LANGUAGE SQL AS 'SELECT a::integer UNION ALL SELECT a::integer + 30'
CREATE FUNCTION scalar_set(a integer DEFAULT nextval('defaults_seen')::integer) RETURNS SETOF integer LANGUAGE SQL VOLATILE AS 'SELECT a UNION ALL SELECT a + 10'
CREATE FUNCTION table_set(a integer) RETURNS TABLE(n integer, label text) LANGUAGE SQL AS 'SELECT a, a::text UNION ALL SELECT a + 1, (a + 1)::text'
CREATE FUNCTION pl_set(a integer) RETURNS SETOF integer LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RETURN NEXT a; RETURN NEXT a + 20; END $$
CREATE FUNCTION checked_set(a integer) RETURNS SETOF accepted_value LANGUAGE SQL AS 'SELECT a'
CREATE FUNCTION strict_set(a integer) RETURNS SETOF integer LANGUAGE plpgsql STRICT AS $$ BEGIN RETURN NEXT a; END $$
CREATE FUNCTION record_set(a integer) RETURNS SETOF record LANGUAGE SQL AS 'SELECT a, a::text'
CREATE TYPE pair AS (n integer, label text)
CREATE FUNCTION pair_set(a integer) RETURNS SETOF pair LANGUAGE SQL AS 'SELECT a, a::text'
SELECT id, scalar_set(v) AS n, pl_set(v) AS p FROM inputs ORDER BY id, n NULLS FIRST, p NULLS FIRST
SELECT i.id, f.n, f.ordinality FROM inputs i CROSS JOIN LATERAL scalar_set(i.v) WITH ORDINALITY AS f(n, ordinality) ORDER BY i.id, f.ordinality
